rubric.why: Identifies the direction condition for like parallel forces.
rubric.description: Like parallel forces act in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both the same-direction condition and the term like parallel forces.

rubric.why: Identifies the direction condition for unlike parallel forces.
rubric.description: Unlike parallel forces act in opposite directions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both the opposite-direction condition and the term unlike parallel forces.

modelAnswer: If the parallel forces are acting in the same direction, then they are called like parallel forces and if their directions are opposite to one another, they are called unlike parallel forces.

rubric.why: Recognises that rectangular components are perpendicular components of a force.
rubric.description: A force is resolved into two components perpendicular to each other, called its perpendicular or rectangular components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the components as perpendicular or rectangular components.

rubric.why: Gives the correct values of both rectangular components.
rubric.description: The x-component is F cos θ and the y-component is F sin θ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for both correct component equations, with the x-component using cosine and the y-component using sine.

modelAnswer: Usually, a force is resolved into two components which are perpendicular to each other. These are called its perpendicular or rectangular components of the force. The x-component of force F is denoted as F_x and y-component as F_y. F_x = F cos θ; F_y = F sin θ.

rubric.why: Identifies the line as the path or direction along which the force acts.
rubric.description: The force acts along a particular line.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the force acts along the line.

rubric.why: Names that line as the line of action of the force.
rubric.description: The line is called the line of action of the force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the term line of action.

modelAnswer: The line along which the force acts is called the line of action of the force.

rubric.why: Provides the textbook example and identifies its constant-velocity motion.
rubric.description: A paratrooper descending with uniform velocity is an example of dynamic equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a paratrooper and stating that the motion is at uniform velocity.

rubric.why: Explains that opposing forces balance in the example.
rubric.description: The downward force of gravity is balanced by the upward air resistance on the parachute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing gravity and air resistance as opposite, balanced forces.

modelAnswer: A good example of dynamic equilibrium is a paratrooper. In a few second after the free fall, the parachute opens and a little later, the paratrooper starts descending with a uniform velocity. In this state, the force of gravity acting vertically downward on the paratrooper is balanced by the resistance of air on the parachute acting upward.

rubric.why: States the defining condition for equilibrium.
rubric.description: A body in equilibrium has no acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a body in equilibrium has no acceleration.

rubric.why: Applies the condition to conclude that an accelerated body is not in equilibrium.
rubric.description: An accelerated body has acceleration and therefore cannot be in equilibrium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the body's acceleration to the conclusion that it cannot be in equilibrium.

modelAnswer: A body is said to be in equilibrium if it has no acceleration. If a body is accelerated, it has acceleration and therefore cannot be in equilibrium.
